title: Chase Wire Transfer Status 'Action Required': Why It's Held & How to Clear It [2026]
content:
When transferring large sums via domestic or international wire—such as home closing costs, vehicle purchases, or commercial vendor settlements—seeing your Chase wire transfer status stall on **"Action Required"** or **"Under Review"** can induce severe anxiety. 

Unlike automated clearing house (ACH) transfers, wire transfers travel across the Federal Reserve Wire Network (Fedwire) or SWIFT. Because wire transfers are irreversible once cleared, Chase’s Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and Global Sanctions algorithms place hard administrative holds on any transaction that exhibits anomalous patterns.

First and foremost: **Your money is not lost.** The funds are temporarily escrowed in an internal Chase general ledger while risk analysts verify sender authorization.

## What Does "Action Required" on a Chase Wire Transfer Mean?

**"Action Required" signifies that Chase has halted the wire to obtain explicit verbal or digital identity confirmation from the account holder.** This hold is triggered by regulatory compliance mandates, recipient name variations against federal sanctions lists, or sudden high-dollar transfers.

| Diagnostic Field | Technical Details |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Transfer Type** | Domestic Fedwire / International SWIFT |
| **Daily Cutoff Window** | 5:00 PM Eastern Time (Domestic Wires) / 4:00 PM ET (International) |
| **Primary Regulatory Drivers** | FinCEN Currency Transaction Reporting, OFAC Sanctions, Reg E |
| **Average Hold Duration** | 2 Hours to 24 Business Hours (until verified) |

> ⚠️ **Security Warning:** Beware of Wire Recall Scams! If you submitted a wire for a real estate closing and receive an incoming phone call or email asking you to "re-route the wire to updated escrow accounts," **DO NOT COMPLY**. Real estate wire interception fraud is at an all-time high. Verify closing instructions in person or via telephone numbers you independently source.

## The 4-Stage Resolution Process (Clear the Hold Before the 5:00 PM Cutoff)

Because domestic wires must clear the Federal Reserve by 5:00 PM Eastern Time for same-day settlement, follow this sequential escalation path immediately:

### Stage 1: Respond to Automated SMS and Email Verification Prompts
In over 60% of flagged transfers, Chase attempts digital self-service clearance before assigning a live analyst:
1. Check your primary mobile phone for an SMS text message originating from Chase shortcode **24273**.
2. The message will specify: *"Chase Security: Did you request a wire transfer of $X to [Recipient Name]? Reply YES or NO."*
3. Reply **YES**. 
4. Check your email for a matching notification from `chase@message.chase.com`. Open the Chase Mobile App and look for a banner alert at the top of your dashboard.
*Once you confirm via SMS, wait 10 to 15 minutes and refresh your Wire Activity screen. The status will often flip from "Action Required" to "Processing".*

### Stage 2: Inspect the Chase Secure Message Center for a Case Reference Number
If [SMS verification](/guides/chase-not-sending-otp-verification-text) is unavailable for your profile:
1. Log into **Chase.com** or the Chase Mobile App.
2. Tap the **Profile / Settings** icon and navigate to **Secure Message Center**.
3. Locate the message titled **"Action required on your wire transfer"**.
4. Note the **10-digit Wire Confirmation Number** and the assigned **Risk Operations Case Number**. You will need these to bypass tier-1 telephone queues.

### Stage 3: Direct Phone Escalation to Chase Global Wire Operations (Phone Tree Bypass)
Do not call the general retail banking number and wait on hold for an hour. Use the dedicated Wire Risk queue:
1. Call the **Chase Wire Operations Department** directly at **1-800-935-9935** (or **1-877-691-8086** for dedicated commercial wire support).
2. When the automated attendant asks for the reason for your call, speak clearly: **"Wire Transfer Status"** or **"Wire Action Required"**.
3. When prompted, enter your 16-digit debit card number and your billing zip code.
4. **Phone Tree Pro-Tip:** If prompted with automated balance updates, press **0#** twice to force transfer to a live Wire Specialist.
5. Provide the specialist with your Wire Confirmation Number. They will ask standard identity verification questions (recent deposit amounts, out-of-wallet security questions) and release the queue hold while you are on the phone.

### Stage 4: In-Branch Wire Specialist Verification (For High-Value Transfers Above $50,000)
For transactions exceeding $50,000, Chase security protocols often prohibit telephone-based releases:
1. Locate your nearest **Chase Branch**.
2. Bring **two forms of government identification** (e.g., Driver's License and US Passport) and your physical debit card.
3. Request to speak with a **Branch Manager** or **Private Client Banker**.
4. The banker can verify your physical presence, confirm your signatures on file, and submit an internal encrypted ticket directly to Executive Fraud Operations to release the wire within minutes.

## Fedwire Cutoff Deadlines You Must Know


> 💡 **Related Chase Bank Solution:** Encountering related issues? Check our verified fix for [Chase Zelle Payment Pending Review: Release Times & How to Clear It](/guides/chase-zelle-payment-pending-review-how-long).


Time sensitivity is paramount when managing wire holds:
* **Domestic Wires (Online/App):** Must be fully cleared by **5:00 PM Eastern Time (Monday through Friday)**. Wires approved after 5:00 PM ET will settle the next business morning.
* **International Consumer Wires:** Must be approved by **4:00 PM Eastern Time**.
* **Weekend Transfers:** Fedwire is closed on Saturdays, Sundays, and Federal Reserve holidays. Wires submitted on weekends remain in an automated holding queue until 7:00 AM Eastern Time on Monday.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

**Can I cancel a Chase wire transfer while it is marked "Action Required"?**
**Yes.** While the wire is under administrative hold, the funds have not yet left Chase's clearinghouse. Go to **Pay & Transfer** > **Wires** > **Wire Activity**, select the transfer, and look for the **"Cancel Transfer"** link. If canceled, funds return immediately to your available balance.

**Why was my wire flagged if I have more than enough money in my account?**
**Wire holds are not based on insufficient funds; they are triggered by fraud and compliance models.** A new recipient account number, an out-of-state routing transit number, or a transaction amount significantly higher than your 90-day average will trigger an automated pause.

**What happens if I don't respond to the "Action Required" notice?**
**If you do not verify the transaction within 24 to 48 business hours, Chase will automatically cancel the wire.** The held funds will be un-escrowed and returned to your checking balance without penalty.

**Are wire transfer fees refunded if the transfer is cancelled?**
**Yes.** Chase automatically refunds the $25 to $40 outgoing wire fee if the transfer is terminated while under administrative review.
